settings.transcription.advancedSettingsD: Fine-tune voice detection and transcription accuracy. Default values work well for most audio.
settings.transcription.advancedSettingsT: These settings control how the AI detects speech in your audio and handles edge cases like silence, short utterances, and repetitive output. Only change these if you're experiencing specific issues with transcription quality.
settings.transcription.vadDesc: Controls how speech is detected and segmented in your audio. Silero VAD runs before transcription to identify speech regions.
settings.transcription.vadThresholdToolt: Controls how confident the model must be that audio contains speech. Lower values detect more speech (including quiet or unclear speech) but may include background noise. Higher values are stricter and may miss soft-spoken content.
settings.transcription.vadThresholdHint: Recommended: 0.30-0.50. Lower = more sensitive (may pick up noise). Higher = stricter (may miss quiet speech).
settings.transcription.vadMinSilenceTool: The minimum duration of silence (in milliseconds) required to split speech into separate segments. Shorter values create more, smaller segments. Longer values keep speech together even with brief pauses.
settings.transcription.vadMinSilenceHint: Recommended: 1500-2500ms. Lower = more segments (split on brief pauses). Higher = fewer segments (keeps speech together).
settings.transcription.vadMinSpeechToolt: Speech segments shorter than this duration (in milliseconds) are discarded. Increase to filter out brief clicks, coughs, or mic bumps. Decrease to keep short utterances like 'yes' or 'no'.
settings.transcription.vadMinSpeechHint: Recommended: 200-500ms. Lower = keep brief utterances. Higher = filter out short sounds.
settings.transcription.vadSpeechPadToolt: Extra padding (in milliseconds) added before and after each detected speech segment. Increase if words are being cut off at the beginning or end of sentences. Decrease for tighter segmentation.
settings.transcription.vadSpeechPadHint: Recommended: 200-500ms. Higher = fewer cut-off words. Lower = tighter segments.
settings.transcription.accuracyDesc: Settings to reduce transcription errors like hallucinated text and repeated phrases.
settings.transcription.hallucinationFilt: Whisper can sometimes generate phantom text during silent sections of audio. This filter detects silence gaps and skips any text the model produces during those gaps. Enable this if you see invented words or phrases during quiet sections.
settings.transcription.hallucinationHint: Enable if you see phantom text during silence. Recommended: 2-3 seconds when enabled. Higher = only filters longer silence gaps.
settings.transcription.repetitionPenalty: Penalizes the model for repeating the same words or phrases. At 1.0, no penalty is applied. Increase to 1.1-1.3 if you see the same phrase repeated multiple times. Values above 1.5 may reduce transcription fluency.
1.0 = off (default). 1.1-1.3 = recommended if seeing repetition. Above 1.5 may hurt quality.

about.title: About OpenTranscribe

about.description: OpenTranscribe transforms your audio and video files into accurate, searchable transcripts using cutting-edge AI models. Built for professional workflows with an intuitive user experience.

about.progressiveWebAppDesc: Works seamlessly across desktop and mobile devices.

settings.session.introText: Configure session and token lifetimes to balance security with user convenience. Shorter durations improve security but may require more frequent re-authentication.
settings.session.accessTokenHelp: Short-lived tokens used for API authentication. Recommended: 15-30 minutes.
settings.session.refreshTokenHelp: Used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication. Recommended: 7-30 days.
settings.session.tokenInfo1: Access tokens are short-lived and automatically refreshed in the background
settings.session.tokenInfo2: Users stay logged in as long as refresh token is valid and they remain active
settings.session.tokenInfo3: Refresh tokens rotate on each use for enhanced security
settings.session.restartRequiredHelp: Token lifetimes only take effect after the backend restarts — session cookies are sized from these values at startup. Every other setting on this page applies immediately.
settings.session.idleTimeoutHelp: Session ends after this much inactivity. Checked when a session refreshes its token rather than on every request, so expiry can lag by up to one access-token lifetime. Set to 0 to disable.
settings.session.absoluteTimeoutHelp: Maximum session lifetime regardless of activity, enforced at the same refresh checkpoint as the idle timeout. Forces re-authentication.
settings.session.maxConcurrentSessionsHe: Maximum number of simultaneous sessions per user. Set to 0 for unlimited.
settings.session.policyOldestDesc: At the limit, the user's oldest session is ended so the new sign-in can proceed.
settings.session.policyRejectDesc: At the limit, the new sign-in is rejected and existing sessions keep running.
settings.localAuth.enableLocalHelp: When off, accounts whose password is stored here can no longer sign in — use this when an external identity provider owns identity. LDAP and SSO are unaffected, and an active super admin is always exempt, so you cannot lock yourself out.
settings.localAuth.selfRegistrationHelp: When disabled, only admins can create new accounts
settings.localAuth.registrationRequiresL: Self-registration creates local password accounts, so it cannot be enabled while local authentication is off. The server rejects this combination — turn one of the two back on before saving.
settings.localAuth.totpHelp: Allow users to set up authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.)
settings.localAuth.requireMfaHelp: When enabled, users must set up MFA on next login
settings.localAuth.mfaBackupCodeCountHel: How many one-time backup codes an MFA enrollment generates
settings.localAuth.mfaTokenExpiryHelp: Lifetime of the half-session issued between password and the second factor
settings.localAuth.lockoutEnabledHelp: When off, failed login attempts are never rate-limited by lockout
settings.localAuth.lockoutProgressiveHel: Each repeated lockout for the same account doubles the wait, up to the maximum below
settings.localAuth.lockoutMaxDurationHel: Ceiling for progressive lockout — repeated offenses never wait longer than this
settings.localAuth.loginBannerEnableHelp: Displays a notice on the login page that every user must acknowledge before signing in (FedRAMP AC-8)

settings.oidc.oidcDescription: This integration supports Keycloak and other OIDC-compliant identity providers including Azure AD, Okta, Auth0, and Google Workspace.
settings.oidc.providerPresetHelp: Fills in the claim path, scopes, and discovery URL shape for a known provider. You can still edit every field afterward.
settings.oidc.presetNoteAuthentik: Authentik marks every account's email as unverified (email_verified: false) regardless of its actual state. Pair this with account approval, or verify new accounts manually, until email is confirmed some other way.
settings.oidc.presetNoteEntra: Entra's groups claim carries object GUIDs, not names — the allow/block lists above must contain GUIDs. Above roughly 150–200 group memberships, Entra replaces the claim with a Graph API reference instead of the group list itself, and login will carry no groups at all.
settings.oidc.presetNoteOkta: Okta does not add group membership to the token by default — add the groups claim to this app's authorization server in the Okta admin console first, or the roles claim will always be empty.
settings.oidc.presetNoteGoogle: Google Workspace does not put group membership in the ID token under any configuration. Every login through this preset has zero roles/groups; use the admin role name only if you plan to promote users manually.
settings.oidc.discoveredClaimsHelp: From Test Connection's most recent result — the token itself is only readable after a real login. Use this to catch a misconfigured roles claim before anyone signs in.
settings.oidc.noClaimsSupported: This provider did not advertise a claims_supported list. That is common (Authentik is one) and does not mean the claim is missing — it means this check cannot confirm it either way.
settings.oidc.rolesClaimAdvertisedYes: "{{claim}}" is advertised — the provider says its tokens can carry this claim.
settings.oidc.rolesClaimAdvertisedNo: "{{claim}}" is NOT in the advertised claims list. Sign-in will likely succeed with everyone unable to be granted admin or admitted by a group rule.
settings.oidc.rolesClaimAdvertisedUnknow: Whether "{{claim}}" is advertised is unknown — this provider did not send a claims_supported list.
settings.oidc.serverUrlPublicHelp: Public URL of the OIDC server (used by browser)
settings.oidc.serverUrlInternalHelp: Internal URL for server-to-server communication (leave empty to use public URL)
settings.oidc.discoveryUrlHelp: Leave empty only for realm-based providers such as Keycloak. For any other OIDC provider, paste its .well-known/openid-configuration URL — this replaces the realm-based URLs entirely.
settings.oidc.realmHelp: Realm name for realm-based providers (or tenant ID for Entra ID)
settings.oidc.realmSupersededHelp: Ignored while a discovery URL is set.
settings.oidc.clientSecretHelp: Leave empty for public clients using PKCE
settings.oidc.clientSecretKeepPlaceholde: Leave blank to keep the current secret
settings.oidc.clientSecretSetHelp: A client secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
settings.oidc.callbackUrlHelp: Must be registered in your OIDC provider's client configuration
settings.oidc.usePkce: Use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)
settings.oidc.usePkceHelp: Recommended for enhanced security. Required for public clients.
settings.oidc.expectedAudiencePlaceholde: Leave empty to use client ID
settings.oidc.adminRoleHelp: Users with this role in their token will be granted admin privileges
settings.oidc.rolesClaimHelp: Dotted claim path. Keycloak: realm_access.roles. Authentik and Okta: groups. Entra ID: roles.
settings.oidc.rolesClaimWarning: Getting this wrong fails silently — everyone can sign in and nobody is granted admin.
settings.oidc.scopesHelp: Space-separated scopes requested at the authorization endpoint. openid is required.
settings.oidc.issuerPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the discovery document's issuer
settings.oidc.issuerHelp: Optional. Only set this when the issuer in your provider's tokens differs from the one it advertises.
settings.pki.advancedConfigurationDesc: PKI authentication requires proper infrastructure setup including certificate management, reverse proxy configuration, and CA certificate distribution. See the documentation for detailed setup instructions.
settings.pki.modeHeaderDesc: Certificate passed via HTTP headers from reverse proxy
settings.pki.modeMutualTlsDesc: Direct certificate verification via TLS handshake
settings.pki.caCertPathHelp: Path to the trusted CA certificate file (PEM format). Can be a CA bundle.
settings.pki.certHeaderHelp: HTTP header containing the client certificate
settings.pki.dnHeaderHelp: HTTP header containing the certificate DN
settings.pki.trustedProxiesHelp: Comma-separated list of trusted proxy IP ranges (CIDR notation)
settings.pki.softFailHelp: When enabled, authentication proceeds if OCSP/CRL servers are unreachable
settings.pki.adminDnsHelp: One DN per line. Users with matching certificate DNs will be granted admin privileges.
settings.pki.allowPasswordFallbackHelp: Deployment-wide ceiling, not a grant: password sign-in works only when this is enabled AND the individual account has local fallback allowed. Leave it enabled unless you intend to revoke fallback from every account at once.
settings.pki.allowPasswordFallbackWarnin: Turning this off revokes password fallback from every account that was granted it individually — including administrators. Make sure a certificate-based administrator can still sign in.
settings.proxy.advancedConfigurationDesc: An authenticating reverse proxy (oauth2-proxy, Authelia, Cloudflare Access) asserts the identity via HTTP headers; this tab decides whether to believe it. Requires the proxy to be the only path that reaches this app — see the documentation for network setup.
settings.proxy.trustedProxiesHelp: Comma-separated list of trusted proxy IP ranges (CIDR notation). Empty refuses every header-sourced assertion — this is fail-closed, the same rule as PKI's trusted proxies field.
settings.proxy.sharedSecretHelp: Optional secret the proxy must send alongside its headers, compared in constant time.
settings.proxy.sharedSecretKeepPlacehold: Leave blank to keep the current secret
settings.proxy.sharedSecretSetHelp: A shared secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or type a new one to replace it. Compared in constant time.
settings.proxy.emailHeaderHelp: HTTP header carrying the authenticated user's email address
settings.proxy.nameHeaderHelp: HTTP header carrying the display name used for JIT-created accounts
settings.proxy.groupsHeaderHelp: HTTP header carrying group names. An absent header means the proxy manages no groups (group reconciliation is skipped entirely); an empty header value means reconcile to no groups — these are different outcomes.
settings.proxy.groupsSeparatorHelp: Separator used inside the groups header. Use a semicolon if the values are DNs, since DNs contain commas.
settings.proxy.roleHeaderHelp: HTTP header carrying the asserted role. Empty means header-driven privilege is off (the default, deliberately: this header grants privilege over HTTP). Capped at admin — super_admin is never reachable through this header, for any value.
settings.proxy.roleHeaderOffNotice: No role header is configured. The proxy cannot grant admin or super_admin privilege through headers; accounts get their default role.
settings.proxy.allowedDomainsHelp: Comma-separated list of email domains permitted to sign in. Empty admits every domain.
settings.proxy.jitProvisioningHelp: When enabled, an unknown asserted identity may be created on the fly. When disabled, only pre-existing accounts can sign in through the proxy.
settings.saml.samlDescription: An external Identity Provider (IdP) asserts identity via signed SAML assertions posted back to this application's Assertion Consumer Service (ACS).
settings.saml.spEntityIdHelp: The unique identifier this application presents to the identity provider as the Service Provider.
settings.saml.spAcsUrlHelp: Where the identity provider posts the SAML assertion back to this application after a successful login.
settings.saml.spSlsUrlHelp: Where the identity provider sends single logout requests and responses.
settings.saml.metadataUrlHelp: Public, unauthenticated URL that publishes this application's SP metadata XML — paste it into your identity provider to configure the connection.
settings.saml.metadataUrlCopyFailed: Could not copy the metadata URL
settings.saml.spX509CertHelp: Public — safe to display. Only required when signing or encryption is enabled.
settings.saml.spPrivateKeyHelp: Private key matching the SP certificate above, used to sign outgoing SAML requests.
settings.saml.spPrivateKeyKeepPlaceholde: Leave blank to keep the current key
settings.saml.spPrivateKeySetHelp: A private key is stored. Leave blank to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
settings.saml.idpEntityIdHelp: The unique identifier the identity provider publishes for itself.
settings.saml.idpSsoUrlHelp: Where this application sends SAML authentication requests.
settings.saml.idpSloUrlHelp: Where this application sends single logout requests.
settings.saml.idpX509CertHelp: The identity provider's own signing certificate — what makes assertion signature verification real. Public, but required before SAML can be enabled at all.
settings.saml.wantAssertionsSignedHelp: Reject assertions that are not signed by the identity provider.
settings.saml.wantMessagesSignedHelp: Reject SAML response messages that are not signed by the identity provider.
settings.saml.signAuthnRequestsHelp: Sign SAML authentication requests sent to the identity provider using the SP private key above.
settings.saml.emailAttributeHelp: SAML assertion attribute name carrying the authenticated user's email address.
settings.saml.nameAttributeHelp: SAML assertion attribute name carrying the display name used for JIT-created accounts.
settings.saml.groupsAttributeHelp: SAML assertion attribute name carrying group/role membership.
settings.saml.adminGroupHelp: Group name that grants the admin role to a user asserted as a member.
settings.saml.allowedGroupsHelp: A login must carry at least one of these values.

settings.saml.blockedGroupsHelp: These values are refused outright, checked before the allowed list.
settings.saml.groupsSemicolonHelp: Separate values with semicolons (;) — not commas, which appear inside directory names.

settings.engineSettings.diarizerRequireS: Only applies when Diarizer Backend is "native". Off (default): if the diar-native sidecar can't serve a request, the job silently falls back to the slower PyAnnote engine and still completes. On: a sidecar failure is retried and then raised as a job failure instead of falling back — use this if you'd rather be alerted that the sidecar is broken than keep transcribing on PyAnnote without knowing.
settings.engineSettings.boundarySmoothin: Collapse 1–3 word wrong-speaker islands at speaker turn boundaries (issue #193). Validated to reduce errors; safe to leave on.
settings.engineSettings.boundaryAcoustic: Re-checks short absorbed backchannels ("yeah", "mm-hmm") by voiceprint and reassigns the correct speaker. Adds a small GPU pass per short word. Relabels existing words only — never invents speech. Experimental (issue #193).
Minimum voiceprint similarity improvement over the current speaker before a word is reassigned. Higher is more conservative (fewer changes). Default 0.05.
Only re-check words at or below this length in seconds — backchannels are short. Default 1.0.
